references.text: Miriam was struck with leprosy that was white as snow, the same description as Moses' hand in Exodus 4:6
Naaman's leprosy is transferred to Gehazi and his descendants, described as white as snow, corresponding to Moses' hand
The continuation of the sign where Moses' hand is healed when he puts it back into his cloak
Moses performs the signs, including the sign with the leprous hand, before the people of Israel
Reminder of leprosy and how God struck Miriam with it, linked to God's power over this disease
The laws concerning leprosy and white spots on the skin, describing the condition Moses' hand received
Typological contrast: God's hand as judge (Moses) vs. God's hand as healer (Jesus).
Fulfillment: Jesus takes on the role of the pure priest who can himself declare purity.
Explanation: Moses' signs demonstrate the specific symptoms (white skin) that the Law defines in Leviticus.
Explanation: The miracle in Exodus fulfills the ritual criteria for uncleanness described here.
Contrast: The Lord's hand as a source of healing (Moses) vs. judgment (Elymas).
Fulfillment: Jesus breaks with the cleansing process required by the Law by himself touching the unclean.
Typological contrast: God's hand brings judgment (Moses) vs. God's hand gives life (Jesus).
Theological development: From God's judgment on uncleanness (Moses) to humanity's plea for purity with Jesus.
